svg.title: Eight frames. The rerun battled every team against all 50 meta files with the six Pokemon shuffled before each battle. An edit changes one thing on one Pokemon, in one of six kinds, and each kind is tried 3 times on a team. Replays of the unchanged team show battle noise, about 3.40 points. With noise removed, one edit moves win rate by 5.90 points for a whole Pokemon swap, 4.84 for a move, 4.35 for an item, 3.66 for an ability, 1.95 for stat alignment and 1.60 for Stat Points. No size cutoff is used. Four kinds have a 95% interval above zero from tournament-ready teams, and the two Stat kinds do not. As a share of the 9.04-point spread between teams, the same four kinds are larger than one step on the Pest Control benchmark, which is 0.14 of its own spread. From search-found teams only the whole Pokemon swap and the move edit hold.

4. A replay: the same team, battled again
A replay shows how far a score moves by luck
alone. That move is battle noise.
The team in frame 2 scored 56.25%, then 52.3%,
53.1% and 52.9% on its 3 replays. A typical replay
5. From scores to a change in points
What we measure after an edit is its real move
plus battle noise. The two are independent, so
they add as squares, like the short sides of a
For the whole Pokemon swap: 6.81 squared minus
would give 3.41 and undercount the edit.
6. Is the edit real? Change in points with its 95% interval, tournament-ready teams
An edit kind is real when its whole interval, the
thin capped line, sits above zero. Four kinds are.
Stat alignment and Stat Points reach zero, so they
The whole Pokemon swap is 5.90 points, interval
4.78 to 7.01. From search-found teams only the

7. Is the edit large? Its share of the spread between teams, against one step on a
The yardstick is a benchmark, not a number someone
picked. Each size is divided by how far teams'
scores spread, 9.04 points. One step on Pest
Control is 0.14 of that benchmark's own spread.
A whole Pokemon swap is 0.65 of the spread, more
than four times the benchmark's step. The four
real kinds are larger than the step. The two Stat
kinds cannot be told apart from it.
8. The two readings, kind by kind
Two kinds are real and larger than the benchmark's
step from both groups of teams: the whole Pokemon
swap and the move edit. Item and ability edits
join them from tournament-ready teams only.
The plan of 2026-09-28 also required a change of
at least 5 points, with no reason for the number,
and under it only the whole Pokemon swap passed.
